text: You have never once felt cold flow into your hand. Cold does not move. Here is what actually happens when you touch an ice cube.

Hi there, and welcome to The One App, Explained! I'm so happy you're here. Today, you will learn three big ideas. First, which way heat flows. Second, when heat stops flowing. And third, how to read a line graph. Let's get started!

Here is the one rule. Heat always flows from a place with a higher temperature, to a place with a lower temperature. Never the other way. So when you hold an ice cube, heat flows out of your warm hand into the ice. Your hand loses heat, so it feels cold. The ice gains heat, so it melts.
That is why, close the door, you are letting the cold out, is backwards. The cold is not leaking out. Heat flows from the warm room into the cold fridge!

Let's try three more. A pot on a stove. The flame is hotter, so heat flows into the pot and the water. A metal spoon in hot coffee. Heat flows from the coffee into the spoon, so the spoon gets hot. And hot tea on the table. Heat flows from the tea to the air around it, so the tea cools down.

But when does heat stop flowing? Put a cup of fifty degree water inside a box of twenty degree water. Heat flows from the hot water to the cool water. The hot water cools, and the cool water warms, until both reach the same temperature. When the temperatures are the same, heat stops flowing. Want to watch heat move? You can try it yourself in The One App. Open the School Lab, experiment seven point one, and press, Let's test it now!

Scientists show this on a line graph. Time goes along the horizontal axis, and temperature goes up the vertical axis. Each measurement is a data point, and a line joins the points. Here, the two lines move towards each other, then become flat when they meet.
Heat also flows within one object. Put one end of a metal rod in a fire, and heat travels along the rod to the cooler end. That is why you should never touch the other end!

Anything that gives off heat is a source of heat. The flame, the hot coffee and the hot tea are all sources of heat. The Sun is our main source of heat. And deep under the ground, the Earth is so hot that it heats up water, making hot springs.
Pause and predict! You hold a cold metal spoon, and it feels cold. Which way did heat flow?
From your hand into the spoon! Your hand lost heat, so it felt cold. No cold moved at all.
In your exam, say it like this. Heat flows from a place of higher temperature to a place of lower temperature, until both are at the same temperature. Never say that cold flows.
Here is a habit for exam answers. Name the direction. Every time you explain heat, say what gains heat, what loses heat, and where the heat flows. It turns a guess into full marks.

Now add to your heat mind map. A branch called heat flow. Hot to cold. Stops when temperatures are equal. Sources of heat, like the Sun and the Earth. Save it in TheOneApp, the ultimate science app. Tap Mind maps, then, Make my own mind map.
So, does cold flow into your hand? Never! Heat flows out of it. Your turn. Next time someone says close the door, you are letting the cold out, explain what is really happening.
Thanks for watching! See you next time. Bye!
